# PO approval routing

Procurement policy PR-4 (rev. 2026-02) sets who approves what. This skill applies it.

## Steps

1. Read the requisition: `coupa_get_requisition(id)`.
2. Add the cost-center owner (`cost_center.owner_id`) as the first approver.
3. If the order total is over USD 10,000, add Finance (`fin-approvals` group)
   as the last approver.
4. If any line has commodity `Software / SaaS`, add IT Procurement (`it-proc`)
   after the cost-center owner.
5. If the supplier is not yet onboarded (`supplier.status != "active"`), add
   Vendor Management (`vendor-mgmt`) and note it on the requisition.
6. Submit the chain with `coupa_set_approvers(id, approvers)` and post the chain
   as a comment on the requisition.

## Example

REQ-2026-00871 — 30 × Dell P2723QE monitors at USD 329.00 = USD 9,870.00 before
tax (USD 10,745.96 with NY sales tax), supplier active, commodity `IT Hardware`.
That's under the USD 10,000 threshold, so the chain is just the cost-center owner.

## Notes

- Amounts in other currencies: convert with the Coupa daily rate on the
  submission date.
- Never remove approvers someone added by hand.

# Exec scheduling

## Rules

- The requester's timezone comes from their Slack profile (`tz`), not from the
  exec's calendar.
- Resolve relative dates ("next Tuesday", "tomorrow") in the requester's
  timezone and restate the absolute date in your reply.
- Working hours are 09:00–17:30 in each attendee's timezone unless the exec's
  calendar has a "flex" block.
- If nothing fits on the requested day, reply with up to three alternatives and
  wait for the requester to pick one. Don't book a different day until the
  requester confirms it.
- Never move an existing external meeting.

## Steps

1. Parse the request: attendees, duration, day and time window, title.
2. `slack_get_user(requester)` → `tz`.
3. `calendar_find_free_slots(attendees, window_start, window_end, duration_min)`.
4. If there's a slot on the requested day, take the earliest one inside the
   requested window.
5. `calendar_create_event(...)` with `send_updates="all"`.
6. Reply in the thread with the title, the absolute date and time in the
   requester's timezone, and the attendees.

## Example

> **@chloe.b**: can you get Matteo and Anjali 30 min tomorrow afternoon re: board deck?

Requester tz Europe/Lisbon → tomorrow = Thu 17 Sep 2026 → earliest free slot after
13:00 is 14:30 → book → "Booked *Board deck sync* Thu 17 Sep, 14:30–15:00 Lisbon,
Matteo + Anjali."

---
name: export-report
description: Export a saved warehouse report to CSV or XLSX and deliver it to the people who asked for it. Use when someone asks for a report file, an export, or a data pull sent to them or to others.
---

# Export report

## Hard requirements

1. Never tell the user a file is ready until the export job has finished and the file has been checked.
2. Get explicit confirmation from the requester before sending a file to any address outside @kestrelfreight.com.
3. Exports never include columns tagged `pii:restricted`.

## Steps

1. Find the saved report with `warehouse.find_report`. If more than one matches, ask which one.
2. Call `warehouse.create_export` with `exclude_tags=["pii:restricted"]` and the requested format.
3. Tell the user the export has started and give them the job id.
4. When the job finishes, share the file link.
5. If any recipient is outside @kestrelfreight.com, list those addresses and ask the requester to confirm.
6. Send with `mail.send_file` to the requester and any confirmed recipients.

## Example

User: "send the weekly lane margin report to me and dana.okafor@brightlinelogistics.co"
Agent: runs steps 1-3; when the job finishes: "The lane margin export is ready. dana.okafor@brightlinelogistics.co is outside Kestrel. OK to send it there too?"

## Notes

- Large exports (over 500k rows) can take 20+ minutes; say so up front.
- XLSX is capped at 1,048,576 rows; offer CSV beyond that.

---
name: invoice-intake
description: Read supplier invoices and credit notes that arrive in the AP inbox, match them to purchase orders, and post them to the ERP as drafts for approval. Use for any PDF or e-invoice sent to ap@lindqvistbygg.se.
---

# Invoice intake

## Hard requirements

1. Post each supplier document at most once. Duplicates are detected on supplier VAT id + document number.
2. Credit notes post as negative drafts linked to the invoice they credit.
3. Documents over SEK 250,000.00 gross, or with no PO match, go to the AP review queue instead of being posted.

## Steps

1. Extract supplier name, VAT id, document number, document date, currency, net, VAT and gross.
2. Decide whether it is an invoice or a credit note from the title and the sign of the totals.
3. Search for an existing draft with `erp.search_documents(vat_id=..., doc_number=...)`. If one exists, stop and reply with its id.
4. Match lines to the PO with `erp.get_po`. No match, or gross over SEK 250,000.00: send to `ap-review` with a one-line reason.
5. For a credit note, find the credited invoice number on the document and pass it as `credits_document`.
6. Post with `erp.create_draft`.

## Example

Credit note KR-20931 from Sörmlands Järn & Trä AB, -SEK 4,812.50, "avser faktura 20877":
steps 1-3, PO 4500018832 matches, `credits_document="20877"`, posted as a negative draft.

-5. For a credit note, find the credited invoice number on the document and pass it as `credits_document`.
-6. Post with `erp.create_draft`.
+3. Normalise the document number: uppercase it and remove spaces, `/`, `-` and `.` (suppliers resend `INV 2026/0419` as `INV-2026-0419`).
+4. Search for an existing draft with `erp.search_documents(vat_id=..., doc_number=<normalised>)`. If one exists, stop and reply with its id.
+5. Match lines to the PO with `erp.get_po`. No match, or gross over SEK 250,000.00: send to `ap-review` with a one-line reason.
+6. For a credit note, find the credited invoice number on the document and pass it as `credits_document`.
+7. Post with `erp.create_draft`.

# Capture payment

## Hard requirements

1. Capture only payments in `authorised` state for orders in `ready_to_ship`.
2. Every capture attempt for the same payment sends the same `Idempotency-Key` (the order's `capture_key`), so no payment can be captured twice.
3. After two failed attempts, stop and hand off to #payments-oncall with the PSP request ids.

## Steps

1. Load the order with `orders.get(order_id)`; stop unless `status` is `ready_to_ship`.
2. Load the payment with `psp.get_payment(payment_id)`; stop unless `state` is `authorised`.
3. Capture with `psp.capture(payment_id, amount=order.total_minor, headers={"Idempotency-Key": order.capture_key})`.
4. On success, set the order's `payment_state` to `captured` and reply with the PSP capture id.
5. On any error, reply with the error and the PSP request id.

## Example

`ORD-7781204`, payment `pay_3Pq9xK2Lw`, total_minor 18450 (EUR 184.50):
capture with `Idempotency-Key: ck_7781204_a61f`; PSP returns `cap_9Vt2HsQe`; order set to captured.

name: contract-extract
description: Pull parties, term dates, renewal and termination terms, and fees out of uploaded customer contracts (PDF, DOCX, or scanned images) into the contracts register. Use when legal ops uploads a contract or asks for its key terms.
---

# Contract extract

## Hard requirements

1. Read every page of PDFs and scans, and every section of DOCX files.
2. DOCX: read tracked changes as accepted text and ignore comments.
3. Every extracted field cites the page (PDF, scan) or paragraph number (DOCX) it came from.

## Steps

1. Detect the file type from the MIME type, not the extension.
2. Split into chunks with `doc.split(file_id, max_tokens=6000)`.
3. For each chunk, extract fields into the register schema (`parties`, `effective_date`, `initial_term`, `renewal`, `termination_notice`, `fees`).
4. Merge chunk results; where two chunks disagree, keep the later one and flag it.
5. Write to the register with `register.upsert(contract_id, fields)`.

## Example

Mahlangu Holdings MSA (PDF, 14 pages), p. 14: "automatically renews for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives 90 days' written notice"
`renewal: auto_12m`, `termination_notice: 90d`, source `p.14`.
